transcript: So I'm not gonna lie to y'all. I really did not love this play. Going into it, I was obviously really excited to see Robert Downey Jr's Broadway debut, but coming out, I was honestly just left very disappointed, not only by his performance, but also just the play in general. This is a show about A I, and that's pretty much as far as the concept goes. It doesn't really do anything interesting with that concept or really explore it beyond just a very surface level. The play itself feels like it is trying to emulate what a play written by AI would be like, which is to say that it is intentionally pulling plot points from other plays and just kind of mashing them all together. It's the end result is something that kind of resembles a play, but also, like, as a whole, just doesn't make a ton of sense. And, well, yes, there are individual elements of this play that you could isolate and are quite good on their own. When put into the totality of the piece, it just doesn't really work. And while I do think that is an interesting experiment, I don't really want to go to a theater and see a play where its main thesis is, isn't this kind of bad? Like, it felt like it was just constantly asking the audience, like, wouldn't you rather be watching a play that was written by a human and made narrative sense? And Was engaging, and I was sitting there like, yes, I would much rather be watching that play. As for the performances, I definitely thought Andrea Martin was the standout, as she often is, but she really isn't given a ton to do. And honestly, no one in the supporting cast is given a ton to do outside of like, one scene for each of them. The only person who really gets a ton of stage time is Robert Downey Jr, who is basically in the play from start to finish. To be honest, I really don't know that there are many reasons to see the show unless you really just want to see Robert Downey Jr. On stage, which you will. He is certainly on that stage delivering lines. I just wish that he and honestly, the rest of the extremely talented supporting cast were given more to work with.
